summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of mitochondrial myopathy, coronary artery disease, and orthostatic hypotension was admitted for atypical chest pain and shortness of breath occurring at rest, consistent with prior episodes triggered by dehydration. Initial evaluation showed no evidence of acute ischemia, with negative troponins and unchanged EKG. The patient reported symptom relief with IV hydration, and orthostatic hypotension resolved during the stay. His cardiac rhythm remained stable on telemetry, with no arrhythmias detected. Kidney function was stable throughout, and a chest X-ray showed no acute pulmonary process. The patient was discharged home in stable condition with no changes to his baseline medications except for continuation of lower-dose aspirin. He was advised to maintain hydration and follow up with his primary care provider and cardiologist to optimize outpatient management and reduce future hospitalizations.
